intro: The biggest thing stopping most first-time buyers isn't the monthly payment. It's the down payment. San Antonio buyers have real help available, and most people never ask for it.
Here's every major program, broken down so you can see in a minute which ones fit you.

items: How it works: a 0% second loan with no monthly payment that is fully forgiven over time (5 years up to $15,000; 10 years above that)
Income limit (2026): $56,350 for 1 person, up to $106,300 for a household of 8
Max price: $260,000 for an existing home, $284,000 for new construction

sections.h2: TSAHC: Homes for Texas Heroes and Home Sweet Texas
items: Help: up to 5% of your loan, as a grant or a second lien
Homes for Texas Heroes: teachers, police, fire and EMS, corrections officers, veterans and active military, and nursing faculty
Home Sweet Texas: for low- and moderate-income buyers

sections.h2: How to use this without getting burned
items: Step 1: get pre-approved with a lender that offers these programs (not every lender does)
Step 2: ask the lender which program gives you the lowest total cost, not just the biggest check
Step 3: take the homebuyer class early if your program requires it
Step 4: pick an agent who has closed with assistance programs; the timelines are tighter

faq.q: How much down payment assistance can I get in San Antonio?
faq.a: The City of San Antonio's HIP 80 offers $1,000 to $30,000 for eligible buyers on homes up to $260,000 (existing). TDHCA and TSAHC programs offer up to 5% of the loan amount.

faq.q: Do I have to be a first-time buyer?
faq.a: Not for every program. TDHCA's My Choice Texas Home doesn't require it, and veterans can be exempt from the first-time rule in My First Texas Home.

faq.q: Is HIP money available right now?
faq.a: It depends on the city's funding at the time. Ask the City of San Antonio or a participating lender before you write an offer.
